intended_object: A residually finite additive group: one in which the intersection of all finite-index normal subgroups is trivial. Equivalently, every nonzero element lies outside some finite-index normal subgroup. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The class asks that the infimum of all finite-index normal additive subgroups be `⊥`. Here `FiniteIndexNormalAddSubgroup` is an additive subgroup that is normal and has `FiniteIndex`, i.e. nonzero index, so finite index. This is the standard definition of a residually finite group, written additively. The definition works for an arbitrary `AddGroup`, which is its natural generality.

It is the additive counterpart of `Group.ResiduallyFinite`. The `@[to_additive]` attribute on the multiplicative class is linked to this declaration, which is written out by hand, and the two have the same shape. In the trivial group the only finite-index normal subgroup is `⊤ = ⊥`, so the condition holds, which is correct. A finite group is also residually finite, since `⊥` itself has finite index.
